chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Sahban, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said to me:
O Muhammad! My father (peace be upon him) used to say: O my son! God has not created anything more delightful to the eye of your father than al-Taqiyyah (concealment of faith).

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أَقَرَّ لِعَيْنِ: More delightful/pleasing to the eye, indicating high value or joy.
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Concealment of faith or dissimulation, a key theological and practical doctrine in Shia Islam.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Taqiyyah in the teachings of the Imams according to al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declaring that 'al-Taqiyyah' is the most delightful characteristic to the Imams, elevating it from a mere survival tactic to a cherished spiritual virtue. This narration underscores the theological significance of dissimulation as a means of preserving the divine truth and the Imams' lineage during periods of political oppression, reflecting the Shia concept of 'hiddenness' (Ghaybah) and continuity of guidance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-78 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abil Sahban, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Jamil ibn Salih, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Marvan who narrated that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) told him, “O Muhammad!
My father said, ‘O my son! God has not created anything more delightful than concealing of faith for your father.’”
